method.name: CurrentTab
method.description: Defines the active tab in the dialog. This property can be overridden by using the showTabs() method.

method.name: GeneralTabCaption
method.description: Defines the label for the first tab in the dialog.

method.name: Name
method.description: Defines the text displayed in the title bar of the dialog.

method.name: addProperty
method.description: Adds a new property to the dialog. If a property with the given name exists, that property is deleted and replaced with the new property. The onchanged argument can be used to call a function for handling property value changes; otherwise give a None value. A tab is added to the dialog when you add a property using the following format for its name argument. [TabName]::[PropertyName] See Property Constants for more information on property types and constraints.
method.parameters: String name, Enumeration type, String onchanged, Enumeration constraints

method.name: destroyWindow
method.description: Hides and destroys the dialog.

method.name: getProperty
method.description: Returns a property of the dialog matching the given name; otherwise returns None.

method.name: hide
method.description: Hides the dialog.

method.name: show
method.description: Shows the dialog.

method.name: showTabs
method.description: Shows the dialog and its tabs. An optional tabName argument can be used to define which tab is listed first and active in the dialog. If there is no tab matching the given tabName or the method is called without any argument, the first listed tab is used in the dialog. By default, the first tab is named General.

method.name: addLimitProperty
method.description:
Adds a property with defined limits to the dialog's owner.
If a property with the given name exists, that property is deleted and replaced with the new property. The onchanged argument can be used to call a function for handling property value changes; otherwise give a None value. A tab is added to the dialog when you add a property using the following format for its name argument. [TabName]::[PropertyName] The rebuild argument can be used to rebuild geometry referencing the property's value; otherwise give a False value. The update argument can be used to update a simulation when changing the property's value; otherwise give a False value. The value argument defines the initial value of the property, whereas the min and max arguments define the property's limits. The units argument can given as an empty string "" or a unit associated with the property's type. To show/hide the property in the dialog, use the visible argument. See Property Constants for more information.
method.parameters: vcCommand owner, Enumeration type, String name, Boolean visible, Boolean rebuild, Boolean update, var* value, String onchanged, var* units, var* min, var* max

method.name: addStepProperty
method.description:
Adds a property with defined values to the dialog's owner.
If a property with the given name exists, that property is deleted and replaced with the new property. The onchanged argument can be used to call a function for handling property value changes; otherwise give a None value. A tab is added to the dialog when you add a property using the following format for its name argument. [TabName]::[PropertyName] The rebuild argument can be used to rebuild geometry referencing the property's value; otherwise give a False value. The update argument can be used to update a simulation when changing the property's value; otherwise give a False value. The value argument defines the initial value of the property, whereas possible values are given as optional values in a list. The units argument can given as an empty string "" or a unit associated with the property's type. To show/hide the property in the dialog, use the visible argument. See Property Constants for more information.
method.parameters: vcCommand owner, Enumeration type, String name, Boolean visible, Boolean rebuild, Boolean update, var* value, String onchanged, var* units, List* [value1, ...]

method.name: displayPropertyDialog
method.description: Shows a modal property dialog bound to a command matching the given cmdName. The cmdName argument is used to find a command owning the dialog and its properties. The title argument defines the caption of the dialog's title bar. The firstTabName argument defines the first and active tab of the dialog. You can given an empty string "" if no tabs are required in the dialog.
method.parameters: String cmdName, String title, String firstTabName

method.name: copyProperties
method.description:
Copies the properties of a component to another component.
The comp1 argument defines the component whose properties are copied. The comp2 argument defines the component which gets the copied properties.

method.name: endMessage
method.description: Prints a given message to the Output panel and unblocks the application.

method.name: findCommand
method.description: Returns a command in the application matching the given name; otherwise returns None.

method.name: progressMessage
method.description:
Prints a given message to the Output panel and updates the value of the progress bar based on a given fraction ranging from 0.0 to 1.0.
Generally, this is used to provide feedback to a user about the progress of one or actions. This method does not unblock the application.

method.name: progressStdMessage
method.description: Displays the status of an operation based on a given amount of work completed in relation to the total amount of work. This method does not unblock the application.

method.name: startMessage
method.description: Prints a given message to the Output panel. Using this method, progressMessage() or progressStdMessage() will block the application, thereby preventing user interaction. To unblock the application, use the endMessage() method.

property.name: getDialog
property.description: Creates a new DialogObject object representing a non-modal dialog box. An option caption argument can be given to define the title caption of the dialog.

method.name: RecordRoutine
method.description: Defines a sequence in the robot where new statements are added when RecordRSL is set to True. This property must be defined before setting RecordRSL to True. By default, new statements are added to the MainRoutine of the robot.

method.name: RecordRSL
method.description: Defines if actions executed by the robot are recorded as statements in the robot's program. If True, statements are added to a routine defined by RecordRoutine.

method.name: SignalMapOut

method.name: delay
method.description: Executes a timed delay (in seconds) and records a Delay statement for this action in the robot's program.

method.name: driveJoints
method.description:
Drives one or more joints in the robot to given target values.
If no value is given for a joint, the current value of the joint is used by the robot. Optional arguments j1 to j6 are target values for joints 1 through 6 in a robot, with six joints being common in articulated robots. An optional motiontime argument can be given to scale the acceleration and speed of the robot's motion to match the given time. The default value is zero in which scaling is disabled. An optional relative argument can be used to set target values as relative to the current value of each joint. The default value is False in which target values are absolute joint values. An optional ExtraJoints argument can be given as a list of joint values for additional joints in a robot, for example external joints of a robot mounted on a track and remotely connected to a workpiece positioner. Tip: Joints can be individually driven by controller; see methods in vcServoController.
method.parameters: [Real j1], [Real j2], [Real j3], [Real j4], [Real j5], [Real j6], [Real motiontime], [Boolean relative], [Real ExtraJoints]

method.name: followNode
method.description: Defines a node in the 3D world to be followed by the robot for a set amount of time. An optional FollowTime argument can be given to set the amount of time the robot should follow the target node. The default value is 1.0/one second.

method.name: getConfigNames
method.description: Returns a list of available configurations by name for the robot.

method.name: graspComponent
method.description: Grasps a given component using robot.

method.name: graspComponents
method.description: Grasps a given list of components using the robot.

method.name: jointMoveRel
method.description: Executes a joint movement relative to the current pose of robot based in active tool's coordinate system. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are translation movements in the XYZ coordinate axes. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are rotation offsets for the XYZ coordinate axes.
method.parameters: [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz]

method.name: jointMoveToComponent
method.description: Executes a joint movement to a given component, which by default is the component's origin. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target orientation. The default value for rotations is zero. An optional ToFrame argument can be used to set the target location to be a Frame feature in a component. A Frame feature can be given as a vcFeature object or referenced by name. An optional OnFace argument can be used to set the target location to be a face of a component's bound box. A bound box face can be referenced by using one of six recognized names (top, bottom, left, right, front, back). If ToFrame and OnFace arguments are given, the method will first try to use ToFrame.
method.parameters: vcNode ToComp, [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [vcFeature/String ToFrame], [String OnFace]

method.name: jointMoveToMtx
method.description: Executes a joint movement to a given target matrix, otherwise the 3D world origin. An optional ToMtx argument defines the target matrix in the selected coordinate system for this method. By default, the identity matrix is based on World origin. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target matrix position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target matrix orientation. The default value for rotations is zero. An optional CS argument can be used to set the coordinate system used for target calculation, which by default is the World coordinate system. The argument can be either "world" or "irobot" which is the robot's coordinate system.
method.parameters: [vcMatrix ToMtx], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [String CS]

method.name: jointMoveToPosition
method.description: Executes a joint movement to a target defined by given XYZ coordinate values and roll, pitch and yaw values based in a given coordinate system. The Tx, Ty and Tz arguments define the target's XYZ coordinate values. The Rx, Ry and Rz arguments define the target's orientation or ABC values. Rx C target value (Roll) Ry B target value (Pitch) Rz A target value (Yaw) The CS argument defines the coordinate system used for target calculation, which default is World coordinate system. The argument can be either "world" or "irobot" which is the robot's coordinate system. After the target is calculated, a point-to-point motion statement is created in the robot's program which uses the robot's first indexed tool frame. The orientation of that tool frame can affect the TargetABC properties of the motion statement.
method.parameters: Real Tx, Real Ty, Real Tz, Real Rx, Real Ry, Real Rz, String CS

method.name: linearMoveRel
method.description: Executes a linear movement relative to the current pose of robot based in active tool's coordinate system. The Tx, Ty and Tz arguments are translation movements in XYZ coordinate axes. The Rx, Ry and Rz arguments are rotation offsets for XYZ coordinate axes.
method.parameters: Real Tx, Real Ty, Real Tz, Real Rx, Real Ry, Real Rz

method.name: linearMoveToComponent
method.description: Executes a linear movement to a given component, which by default is the component's origin. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target orientation. The default value for rotations is zero. An optional ToFrame argument can be used to set the target location to be a Frame feature in a component. A Frame feature can be given as a vcFeature object or referenced by name. An optional OnFace argument can be used to set the target location to be a face of a component's bound box. A bound box face can be referenced by using one of six recognized names (top, bottom, left, right, front, back). If ToFrame and OnFace arguments are given, the method will first try to use ToFrame.
method.parameters: vcNode ToComp, [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [vcFeature/String ToFrame], [String OnFace]

method.name: linearMoveToMtx
method.description: Executes a linear movement to a given target matrix, otherwise the 3D world origin. An optional ToMtx argument defines the target matrix in the selected coordinate system for this method. By default, the identity matrix is based on World origin. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target matrix position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target matrix orientation. The default value for rotations is zero. An optional CS argument can be used to set the coordinate system used for target calculation, which by default is the World coordinate system. The argument can be either "world" or "irobot" which is the robot's coordinate system.
method.parameters: [vcMatrix ToMtx], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [String CS]

method.name: linearMoveToMtx_ExternalBase
method.description: Executes a linear movement to a given target matrix based in given node's coordinate system. Generally, this method is used when a robot needs to motion to a moving part, for example a pallet on a conveyor. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target matrix position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target matrix orientation. The default value for rotations is zero.
method.parameters: vcNode Basenode, vcMatrix ToMtx, [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz]

method.name: linearMoveToPosition
method.description: Executes a linear movement to a target defined by given XYZ coordinate values and roll, pitch and yaw values based in a given coordinate system. The Tx, Ty and Tz arguments define the target's XYZ coordinate values. The Rx, Ry and Rz arguments define the target's orientation or ABC values. Rx C target value (Roll) Ry B target value (Pitch) Rz A target value (Yaw) The CS argument defines the coordinate system used for target calculation, which default is World coordinate system. The argument can be either "world" or "irobot" which is the robot's coordinate system. After the target is calculated, a linear motion statement is created in the robot's program which uses the robot's first indexed tool frame. The orientation of that tool frame can affect the TargetABC properties of the motion statement.
method.parameters: Real Tx, Real Ty, Real Tz, Real Rx, Real Ry, Real Rz, String CS

method.name: mountTool
method.description: Mounts a given component to flange node of robot.

method.name: moveAway
method.description: Executes a linear retraction movement relative to current pose of robot. An optional Tz argument can be given to set retraction distance, which by default is 200.

method.name: pick
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for robot to pick a given component. Action 1 Robot executes a joint movement based on target component origin and Approach, OnFace and ApproachAxis values. Action 2 Robot executes a linear movement to target component based on OnFace value. Action 3 Target component is grabbed by robot. Action 4 Robot executes a linear retraction movement based on Approach value. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, the robot will use an approach distance of 200 aligned to Z-axis in order to pick from the top face of a given component's bound box. The pick location can be offset using the optional Tx, Ty, Tz, Rx, Ry, and Rz arguments. An optional OnFace argument allows you to set which face of Part bound box to use for Action 2. An optional ApproachAxis argument sets the axis of alignment.
method.parameters: vcComponent Part, [Real Approach], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [String OnFace], [String ApproachAxis]

method.name: pickFromPallet
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for the robot to pick a component from a given Pallet. Action 1 Get a list of components attached to Pallet. That is, a list of child components. Action 2 Select child component to pick based on InversedOrder and Index values. Action 3 Robot executes a joint movement based on child component origin and Approach value. Action 4 Robot executes a linear movement to top face of child component. Action 5 Child component is grabbed by robot. Action 6 Robot executes a linear retraction movement based on Approach value. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, the robot will use an approach distance of 200 to pick the last component of a list of child components for Pallet. An optional Approach argument can be used to change the approach and retract distance used by robot. An optional InversedOrder argument can be used to reverse the list of child components acquired in Action 1. A True value reverses the order, so last component attached to Pallet is first in list. The default value is False. An optional Index argument can be used to select which child component of Pallet is picked by robot. The default value is -1, so last component in Action 1 child components list.

method.name: pickMovingPart
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for the robot to pick a given component that is not stationary. Action 1 Robot executes joint movement based on target component origin and Approach value. Action 2 Robot executes linear movement to top face of target component bound box. Action 3 Target component is grabbed by robot. Action 4 Robot executes a linear retraction movement based on Approach value. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, the robot will use an approach distance of 200 and calculate motion targets based on speed of Part. The pick location can be offset using the optional Tx, Ty, Tz, Rx, Ry, and Rz arguments.
method.parameters: vcComponent Part, [Real Approach], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz]

method.name: place
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for the robot to place a grasped component at a given component. Action 1 Robot executes joint movement based on ToComp origin, Approach and ApproachAxis values. Action 2 Robot executes linear movement to top face of ToComp. Action 3 Grasped component is released by robot to ToComp. Action 4 Robot executes a linear retraction movement based on Approach value. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, a robot will use an approach distance of 200 and the bound box of grasped component to calculate motion targets. The place location can be offset using optional Tx, Ty, Tz, Rx, Ry, and Rz arguments. An optional Part argument can be used to define which component is placed to ToComp. The default is the first component listed in robot's GraspContainer. An optional ApproachAxis argument can be used to define the axis of alignment.
method.parameters: vcComponent ToComp, [Real Approach], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [vcComponent Part], [String ApproachAxis]

method.name: placeInPattern
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for the robot to place components in a given pattern. Action 1 Robot executes joint movement to ToComp. Action 2 Robot executes linear movement to place location. Action 3 Grasped component is released by robot to ToComp. Action 4 Robot executes linear retraction movement away from place location. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, a robot will use an approach distance of 200, the bound box of grasped component and the given pattern to calculate motion targets. The X_index, Y_index and Z_index arguments define the index position for placing a component based on pattern size. The PatternSize_X, PatternSize_Y and PatternSize_Z arguments define the pattern size. An optional ApproachAxis argument can be used to define the axis of alignment. An optional Part argument can be used to define which component is placed to ToComp. The default is the first component listed in robot's GraspContainer. Optional StepSizeX, StepSizeY and StepSizeZ arguments can be used to define the pattern step size for XYZ axes. The default step size values are length, width and height of Part. An optional Rz argument can be used to define a Z-axis rotation offset for place location.
method.parameters: vcComponent ToComp, Integer X_index, Integer Y_index, Integer Z_index, Integer PatternSize_X, PatternSize_Y, Integer PatternSize_Z, [Real Approach], [vcComponent Part], [Real StepSizeX], [Real StepSizeY], [Real StepSizeZ], [Real Rz]

method.name: releaseAllComponents
method.description: Attaches all components of robot's GraspContainer to a given node or container type behavior. If ToObject is a component, a target container is searched for automatically in the component. If not found, the components are directly attached to the given node.

method.name: releaseComponent
method.description:
Attaches a component to a given node or container type behavior.
If ToObject is a component, a target container is searched for automatically in the component. If not found, the released component is directly attached to the given node. The ReleaseThis argument is the component to be detached from robot; otherwise the method will search the robot's GraspContainer.

method.name: rsl_BinIn
method.description: Waits for a signal mapped to a given port to have the given value. The Index argument defines the port in the robot's inputs, Boolean Signal Map behavior. The Value argument defines the value that should be received at the port in order to complete execution. If RecordRSL is set to True, this action is recorded as a new input statement in the robot's program.

method.name: rsl_BinOut
method.description: Sends a given value to a signal mapped to a given port. The Index argument defines the port in the robot's outputs, Boolean Signal Map behavior. The Value argument defines the value that should be sent to the mapped signal. If RecordRSL is set to True, this action is recorded as a new output statement in the robot's program.

method.name: traceOff
method.description: Turns off the tracing of the robot's motions at given tool frame. The Index argument defines the index position of a tool frame in the robot's Tools which is mapped to a port used for tracing.

method.name: traceOn
method.description:
Turns on the tracing of the robot's motions at given tool frame.
The Index argument defines the index position of a tool frame in the robot's Tools which is mapped to a port used for tracing.

method.name: unmountTool
method.description: Dismounts a tool mounted on the robot to either a container type behavior or component. The Tool argument needs to be a tool component mounted on the robot.
method.parameters:
vcComponent Tool, vcContainer ToObject
or vcComponent Tool, vcComponent ToObject

method.name: getSelectedRobotsData
method.description: Returns a list of data for the currently selected robot component in the 3D world. The list of data contains the following: robot program, current routine, robot controller, name of active base frame, name of active tool frame, list of names for all base frames, list of names for all tool frames, index of current configuration, and list of names for all configurations.

method.name: printMatrix
method.description: Prints a given matrix in a clear, readable format to the Output panel.

property.name: getRobot
property.description: Creates a new vcRobot object for a given component which must have a robot executor. One option is to give the name of an interface a robot is connected to in a component as an argument, for example a robot mounted on a pedestal. If found, the robot connected at the interface is used by the constructor. A second option is to give the component of a robot you want to program as an argument. A third option is to not give any argument, thereby a component owning the script is used by the constructor.
property.access: String interface_name or vcComponent robot_component or [no argument]

method.name: RecordRoutine
method.description: Defines a sequence in the robot where new statements are added when RecordRSL is set to True. This property must be defined before setting RecordRSL to True. You can refer to the main routine of robot program as 'MainRoutine', the name of an existing subroutine, or give a name for a new subroutine that will be created during the recording.

method.name: RecordRSL
method.description: Defines if actions executed by the robot are recorded as statements in the robot's program. If True, statements are added to a routine defined by RecordRoutine.

method.name: SignalMapIn
method.description: Gets the Boolean Signal Map behavior used for robot inputs.

method.name: SignalMapOut
method.description: Gets the Boolean Signal Map behavior used for robot outputs.

method.name: Speed
method.description: Defines the Cartesian speed used by the robot for linear movements.

method.name: Tools
method.description: Gets a list of the robot's tool frames.

method.name: callSubRoutine
method.description: Calls a predefined routine by name in the robot's program.

method.name: comment
method.description: Prints a given comment to the Output panel and records a Comment statement for this action in the robot's program.

method.name: delay
method.description: Executes a timed delay (in seconds) and records a Delay statement for this action in the robot's program.

method.name: driveJoints
method.description:
Drives one or more joints in the robot to given target values.
If no value is given for a joint, the current value of the joint is used by the robot. Optional arguments j1 to j6 are target values for joints 1 through 6 in a robot, with six joints being common in articulated robots. An optional motiontime argument can be given to scale the acceleration and speed of the robot's motion to match the given time. The default value is zero in which scaling is disabled. An optional relative argument can be used to set target values as relative to the current value of each joint. The default value is False in which target values are absolute joint values. An optional ExtraJoints argument can be given as a list of joint values for additional joints in a robot, for example external joints of a robot mounted on a track and remotely connected to a workpiece positioner. Tip: Joints can be individually driven by controller; see methods in vcServoController.
method.parameters: [Real j1], [Real j2], [Real j3], [Real j4], [Real j5], [Real j6], [Real motiontime], [Boolean relative], [Real ExtraJoints]

method.name: followNode
method.description: Defines a node in the 3D world to be followed by the robot for a set amount of time. An optional FollowTime argument can be given to set the amount of time the robot should follow the target node. The default value is 1.0/one second.

method.name: getConfigNames
method.description: Returns a list of available configurations by name for the robot.

method.name: graspComponent
method.description: Grasps a given component using robot.

method.name: graspComponents
method.description: Grasps a given list of components using the robot.

method.name: jointMoveRel
method.description: Executes a joint movement relative to the current pose of robot based in active tool's coordinate system. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are translation movements in the XYZ coordinate axes. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are rotation offsets for the XYZ coordinate axes.
method.parameters: [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz]

method.name: jointMoveToComponent
method.description: Executes a joint movement to a given component, which by default is the component's origin. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target orientation. The default value for rotations is zero. An optional ToFrame argument can be used to set the target location to be a Frame feature in a component. A Frame feature can be given as a vcFeature object or referenced by name. An optional OnFace argument can be used to set the target location to be a face of a component's bound box. A bound box face can be referenced by using one of six recognized names (top, bottom, left, right, front, back). If ToFrame and OnFace arguments are given, the method will first try to use ToFrame.
method.parameters: vcNode ToComp, [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [vcFeature/String ToFrame], [String OnFace]

method.name: jointMoveToMtx
method.description: Executes a joint movement to a given target matrix, otherwise the 3D world origin. An optional ToMtx argument defines the target matrix in the selected coordinate system for this method. By default, the identity matrix is based on World origin. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target matrix position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target matrix orientation. The default value for rotations is zero. An optional CS argument can be used to set the coordinate system used for target calculation, which by default is the World coordinate system. The argument can be either "world" or "irobot" which is the robot's coordinate system.
method.parameters: [vcMatrix ToMtx], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [String CS]

method.name: jointMoveToPosition
method.description: Executes a joint movement to a target defined by given XYZ coordinate values and roll, pitch and yaw values based in a given coordinate system. The Tx, Ty and Tz arguments define the target's XYZ coordinate values. The Rx, Ry and Rz arguments define the target's orientation or ABC values. Rx C target value (Roll) Ry B target value (Pitch) Rz A target value (Yaw) The CS argument defines the coordinate system used for target calculation, which default is World coordinate system. The argument can be either "world" or "irobot" which is the robot's coordinate system. After the target is calculated, a point-to-point motion statement is created in the robot's program which uses the robot's first indexed tool frame. The orientation of that tool frame can affect the TargetABC properties of the motion statement.
method.parameters: Real Tx, Real Ty, Real Tz, Real Rx, Real Ry, Real Rz, String CS

method.name: linearMoveRel
method.description: Executes a linear movement relative to the current pose of robot based in active tool's coordinate system. The Tx, Ty and Tz arguments are translation movements in XYZ coordinate axes. The Rx, Ry and Rz arguments are rotation offsets for XYZ coordinate axes.
method.parameters: Real Tx, Real Ty, Real Tz, Real Rx, Real Ry, Real Rz

method.name: linearMoveToComponent
method.description: Executes a linear movement to a given component, which by default is the component's origin. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target orientation. The default value for rotations is zero. An optional ToFrame argument can be used to set the target location to be a Frame feature in a component. A Frame feature can be given as a vcFeature object or referenced by name. An optional OnFace argument can be used to set the target location to be a face of a component's bound box. A bound box face can be referenced by using one of six recognized names (top, bottom, left, right, front, back). If ToFrame and OnFace arguments are given, the method will first try to use ToFrame.
method.parameters: vcNode ToComp, [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [vcFeature/String ToFrame], [String OnFace]

method.name: linearMoveToMtx
method.description: Executes a linear movement to a given target matrix, otherwise the 3D world origin. An optional ToMtx argument defines the target matrix in the selected coordinate system for this method. By default, the identity matrix is based on World origin. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target matrix position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target matrix orientation. The default value for rotations is zero. An optional CS argument can be used to set the coordinate system used for target calculation, which by default is the World coordinate system. The argument can be either "world" or "irobot" which is the robot's coordinate system.
method.parameters: [vcMatrix ToMtx], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [String CS]

method.name: linearMoveToMtx_ExternalBase
method.description: Executes a linear movement to a given target matrix based in given node's coordinate system. Generally, this method is used when a robot needs to motion to a moving part, for example a pallet on a conveyor. Optional arguments Tx, Ty and Tz are offsets for target matrix position. The default value for translations is zero. Optional arguments Rx, Ry and Rz are offsets for target matrix orientation. The default value for rotations is zero.
method.parameters: vcNode Basenode, vcMatrix ToMtx, [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz]

method.name: linearMoveToPosition
method.description: Executes a linear movement to a target defined by given XYZ coordinate values and roll, pitch and yaw values based in a given coordinate system. The Tx, Ty and Tz arguments define the target's XYZ coordinate values. The Rx, Ry and Rz arguments define the target's orientation or ABC values. Rx C target value (Roll) Ry B target value (Pitch) Rz A target value (Yaw) The CS argument defines the coordinate system used for target calculation, which default is World coordinate system. The argument can be either "world" or "irobot" which is the robot's coordinate system. After the target is calculated, a linear motion statement is created in the robot's program which uses the robot's first indexed tool frame. The orientation of that tool frame can affect the TargetABC properties of the motion statement.
method.parameters: Real Tx, Real Ty, Real Tz, Real Rx, Real Ry, Real Rz, String CS

method.name: mountTool
method.description: Mounts a given component to flange node of robot.

method.name: moveAway
method.description: Executes a linear retraction movement relative to current pose of robot. An optional Tz argument can be given to set retraction distance, which by default is 200.

method.name: pick
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for robot to pick a given component. Action 1 Robot executes a joint movement based on target component origin and Approach, OnFace and ApproachAxis values. Action 2 Robot executes a linear movement to target component based on OnFace value. Action 3 Target component is grabbed by robot. Action 4 Robot executes a linear retraction movement based on Approach value. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, the robot will use an approach distance of 200 aligned to Z-axis in order to pick from the top face of a given component's bound box. The pick location can be offset using the optional Tx, Ty, Tz, Rx, Ry, and Rz arguments. An optional OnFace argument allows you to set which face of Part bound box to use for Action 2. An optional ApproachAxis argument sets the axis of alignment.
method.parameters: vcComponent Part, [Real Approach], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [String OnFace], [String ApproachAxis]

method.name: pickFromPallet
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for the robot to pick a component from a given Pallet. Action 1 Get a list of components attached to Pallet. That is, a list of child components. Action 2 Select child component to pick based on InversedOrder and Index values. Action 3 Robot executes a joint movement based on child component origin and Approach value. Action 4 Robot executes a linear movement to top face of child component. Action 5 Child component is grabbed by robot. Action 6 Robot executes a linear retraction movement based on Approach value. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, the robot will use an approach distance of 200 to pick the last component of a list of child components for Pallet. An optional Approach argument can be used to change the approach and retract distance used by robot. An optional InversedOrder argument can be used to reverse the list of child components acquired in Action 1. A True value reverses the order, so last component attached to Pallet is first in list. The default value is False. An optional Index argument can be used to select which child component of Pallet is picked by robot. The default value is -1, so last component in Action 1 child components list.

method.name: pickMovingPart
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for the robot to pick a given component that is not stationary. Action 1 Robot executes joint movement based on target component origin and Approach value. Action 2 Robot executes linear movement to top face of target component bound box. Action 3 Target component is grabbed by robot. Action 4 Robot executes a linear retraction movement based on Approach value. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, the robot will use an approach distance of 200 and calculate motion targets based on speed of Part. The pick location can be offset using the optional Tx, Ty, Tz, Rx, Ry, and Rz arguments.
method.parameters: vcComponent Part, [Real Approach], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz]

method.name: place
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for the robot to place a grasped component at a given component. Action 1 Robot executes joint movement based on ToComp origin, Approach and ApproachAxis values. Action 2 Robot executes linear movement to top face of ToComp. Action 3 Grasped component is released by robot to ToComp. Action 4 Robot executes a linear retraction movement based on Approach value. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, a robot will use an approach distance of 200 and the bound box of grasped component to calculate motion targets. The place location can be offset using optional Tx, Ty, Tz, Rx, Ry, and Rz arguments. An optional Part argument can be used to define which component is placed to ToComp. The default is the first component listed in robot's GraspContainer. An optional ApproachAxis argument can be used to define the axis of alignment.
method.parameters: vcComponent ToComp, [Real Approach], [Real Tx], [Real Ty], [Real Tz], [Real Rx], [Real Ry], [Real Rz], [vcComponent Part], [String ApproachAxis]

method.name: placeInPattern
method.description: Executes a sequence of actions in order for the robot to place components in a given pattern. Action 1 Robot executes joint movement to ToComp. Action 2 Robot executes linear movement to place location. Action 3 Grasped component is released by robot to ToComp. Action 4 Robot executes linear retraction movement away from place location. All three motions executed by the robot are created dynamically during a simulation. By default, a robot will use an approach distance of 200, the bound box of grasped component and the given pattern to calculate motion targets. The X_index, Y_index and Z_index arguments define the index position for placing a component based on pattern size. The PatternSize_X, PatternSize_Y and PatternSize_Z arguments define the pattern size. An optional ApproachAxis argument can be used to define the axis of alignment. An optional Part argument can be used to define which component is placed to ToComp. The default is the first component listed in robot's GraspContainer. Optional StepSizeX, StepSizeY and StepSizeZ arguments can be used to define the pattern step size for XYZ axes. The default step size values are length, width and height of Part. An optional Rz argument can be used to define a Z-axis rotation offset for place location.
method.parameters: vcComponent ToComp, Integer X_index, Integer Y_index, Integer Z_index, Integer PatternSize_X, PatternSize_Y, Integer PatternSize_Z, [Real Approach], [vcComponent Part], [Real StepSizeX], [Real StepSizeY], [Real StepSizeZ], [Real Rz]

method.name: releaseAllComponents
method.description: Attaches all components of robot's GraspContainer to a given node or container type behavior. If ToObject is a component, a target container is searched for automatically in the component. If not found, the components are directly attached to the given node.

method.name: releaseComponent
method.description:
Attaches a component to a given node or container type behavior.
If ToObject is a component, a target container is searched for automatically in the component. If not found, the released component is directly attached to the given node. The ReleaseThis argument is the component to be detached from robot; otherwise the method will search the robot's GraspContainer.

method.name: rsl_BinIn
method.description: Waits for a signal mapped to a given port to have the given value. The Index argument defines the port in the robot's inputs, Boolean Signal Map behavior. The Value argument defines the value that should be received at the port in order to complete execution. If RecordRSL is set to True, this action is recorded as a new input statement in the robot's program.

method.name: rsl_BinOut
method.description: Sends a given value to a signal mapped to a given port. The Index argument defines the port in the robot's outputs, Boolean Signal Map behavior. The Value argument defines the value that should be sent to the mapped signal. If RecordRSL is set to True, this action is recorded as a new output statement in the robot's program.

method.name: traceOff
method.description: Turns off the tracing of the robot's motions at given tool frame. The Index argument defines the index position of a tool frame in the robot's Tools which is mapped to a port used for tracing.

method.name: traceOn
method.description:
Turns on the tracing of the robot's motions at given tool frame.
The Index argument defines the index position of a tool frame in the robot's Tools which is mapped to a port used for tracing.

method.name: unmountTool
method.description: Dismounts a tool mounted on the robot to either a container type behavior or component. The Tool argument needs to be a tool component mounted on the robot.
method.parameters:
vcComponent Tool, vcContainer ToObject
or vcComponent Tool, vcComponent ToObject

method.name: getSelectedRobotsData
method.description: Returns a list of data for the currently selected robot component in the 3D world. The list of data contains the following: robot program, current routine, robot controller, name of active base frame, name of active tool frame, list of names for all base frames, list of names for all tool frames, index of current configuration, and list of names for all configurations.

method.name: printMatrix
method.description: Prints a given matrix in a clear, readable format to the Output panel.

property.name: getRobot
property.description: Creates a new vcRobot object for a given component which must have a robot executor. One option is to give the name of an interface a robot is connected to in a component as an argument, for example a robot mounted on a pedestal. If found, the robot connected at the interface is used by the constructor. A second option is to give the component of a robot you want to program as an argument. A third option is to not give any argument, thereby a component owning the script is used by the constructor.
property.access: String interface_name or vcComponent robot_component or [no argument]
